title: 2005 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: How many distinct four-tuples \((a, b, c, d)\) of rational numbers are there with \[ \begin{aligned} &a\log_{10} 2 + b\log_{10} 3 \\ &\quad {}+ c\log_{10} 5 + d\log_{10} 7 = 2005? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
The equation is equivalent to \(\log_{10}\left(2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d\right) = 2005,\) so \[ 2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d = 10^{2005} = 2^{2005} \cdot 5^{2005}. \]

Clearing the denominators of \(a, b, c, d\) with a common integer multiplier and using the uniqueness of prime factorization, the exponents must match: \(a = 2005,\) \(b = 0,\) \(c = 2005,\) and \(d = 0.\)

So there is exactly \(1\) such four-tuple.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Then \(2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d = 10^{2005} = 2^{2005}5^{2005}\); match exponents via unique factorization
